title: AUDIBLE: A Convolution-Based Resource Allocator for Oversubscribing Burstable Virtual Machines
problem: Efficiently allocating resources to burstable virtual machines while maximizing datacenter utilization. Traditional fixed oversubscription ratios and Central Limit Theorem approaches fail for BVMs, resulting in either low utilization or high server capacity violations.
motivation: Cloud providers need better resource allocation strategies for burstable VMs to increase datacenter utilization while maintaining reliability guarantees.
method: AUDIBLE predicts how much resources each burstable virtual machine needs using a convolution-based statistical model—a mathematical technique that combines probability distributions without assuming a specific shape. Because it's non-parametric (requires no parameter tuning), it avoids the computational overhead of training machine learning models. The method works regardless of the workload pattern and was validated through extensive simulations using real production data from a major cloud provider.
key_novelty: Instead of machine learning, it uses a convolution-based statistical model (a technique that combines probability distributions) to predict resources for burstable virtual machines without requiring model training.
contributions: First characterization of burstable VM workload characteristics using production cloud traces
Empirical analysis demonstrating inadequacy of traditional fixed-ratio and CLT-based allocation approaches for BVMs
AUDIBLE: lightweight, non-parametric statistical scheduling algorithm for burstable VMs
Validation showing high utilization with stringent capacity violation guarantees

metrics.other: system utilization and server capacity violation rate

primary_theme: Resource allocation for cloud burstable virtual machines
